subject: Re: Signet maintenance window / upgrade coordination for private deployment
messages:
From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acmehealth.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: ops@cloudopssol.com
Date: 2026-12-20T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Signet maintenance window / upgrade planning

Hi Mina,

We're starting to plan the quarterly maintenance for our private Redwood deployment (Signet cluster). We have a hard constraint of a 2-hour window during off-hours (we prefer Sat/Sun UTC) for any disruption. Can you share your proposed upgrade sequence and any rollback guarantees? Important constraints from our side: no HSM key rotations during the window, audit logging must remain intact (we need last 90 days preserved), and we cannot accept more than 1% request error spike.

Also please confirm whether model-serving version pinning will prevent a multi-version mix during canary, and how KV-cache warms are handled so inference latency doesn't spike on first requests.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Jones
Platform Owner, Acme Health

Subject: Re: Signet maintenance window / upgrade planning

Hi Sara — thanks for the heads up. Below is a proposed plan that tries to respect the 2-hour disruption SLA while giving us safe rollback options. High level summary first, then a short runbook and ask list. Attached: upgrade-checklist.xlsx and canary-rollout-diagram.png.

Summary (what we will change)
- Runtime: inference-engine 2.14 -> 2.17 (includes attention kernel fallback)
- GPU driver: NVIDIA 535.x -> 540.x (driver package + libcuda)
- System: minor kernel patch (no ABI changes)
- Model-serving artifact: pinned via image tag + immutable manifest (we will not auto-mix versions)
- KV cache: pre-warm step on canary nodes; prefix caching applied for hot models

Canary strategy
- 5% traffic routed to Canary zone (Zone-B) for 30 minutes health window
- Health criteria: 99% successful token responses, P95 latency within +15% of baseline, no >1% error spike
- If canary passes, we rollout in two waves (30% then remaining 65%) with a 15-min gating period between waves

Rollback guarantees and mechanics
- Image pinning: we will keep previous image manifest in the private registry for immediate redeploy
- Control-plane toggle: runtime.fallback.enabled flips to previous-image and triggers orchestrated rollback (expected convergence < 6 minutes for stateless pods; < 12 minutes for stateful pieces requiring cache eviction)
- Network-level fallback: we will maintain a traffic-splitting policy at the LB layer to shift traffic off rollout nodes if needed
- Snapshots: we will take config snapshots and etcd backup before start

Proposed window (please confirm):
- Saturday 2026-12-26 02:00 — 05:00 UTC (2-hour disruption target; plan up to 3 hours for safety)

Runbook (short)
1) Preflight (T-48h): config snapshot, registry retention check, DocuSign signed SLA addendum uploaded.
2) Pre-warm (T-2h): pre-pull images to all nodes, warm KV cache on Canary nodes only.
3) Start canary (T+0): route 5% traffic to canary; monitor metrics dashboard and audit logs streaming.
4) Evaluate (T+30m): pass/fail gate. If fail -> trigger runtime.fallback.enabled + LB drain (rollback).
5) Wave rollout: 30% -> 65% with 15m gates.
6) Post-check (T+2h): run synthetic inference test suite, validate audit logs, mark complete.

Compliance notes
- Audit logs: will be forwarded to your SIEM in real time; we will not drop existing logs.
- HSM keys: we will not rotate or rekey during the window.

Asks from Acme
- Confirm the proposed Saturday window (or propose an alternate)
- Confirm that CloudOps (ops@cloudopssol.com) is allowed to change egress firewall rules during pre-warm if needed
- Provide any blackout times or internal calendar conflicts

I'll be available on the 26th and we can provide a 1-hour heads-up SMS before we start. If that works I'll get Marissa to schedule the maintenance bridge and Dev to prep the rollback snippets.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Signet maintenance window / upgrade planning -- rollback snippet

Adding the practical rollback commands and checkpoints we'll run if canary fails. These will be posted to the bridge and to our runbook pages.

Immediate rollback (canary fail)
- Toggle: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/feature-flags/runtime.fallback.enabled -d '{"value":true}'  # triggers orchestrator to redeploy previous manifests
- LB: api call to shift traffic away from Zone-B -> shift % to Zone-A (we automate this).
- K8s (if manual): kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/inference-runtime --to-revision=<previous>
- State: run etcd snapshot restore if a config mutation introduced corruption (only if verification fails).

Pre-checks we will run before starting:
- Verify image retention: curl registry.internal/v2/signet/tags/list -> ensure previous tag exists
- Disk snapshot for stateful sets: create volume snapshot (CSI) and verify size/hash
- Audit log tailing: make sure events are streaming to SIEM and there are no >30s delays

Notes on KV warmup: we will run a scripted warmup that primes the LRU cache with the top-100 active model prefixes to reduce cold-start p95. This lives in the upgrade-checklist.xlsx under step T-30m.

If we hit an unexpected persistent error during the wave, we plan to shelve the new pins (bring both clusters back to the previous image) and then schedule a follow-up hotfix window.

Dev Patel
SRE, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
